A. Does recent evidence support the size of effect we assume: does this measure raise the share of lung cancer patients who get curative-intent treatment, and by how much?
Measure: Video MDT review of every stage I-III patient with the university hospital. Every patient whose cancer has not spread (stage I-III) is discussed by video with the university hospital lung team (surgeon, radiotherapy doctor, oncologist) before anyone decides against treatment that aims to cure. Today a county hospital can decide alone.
effect_summary_en: In one English district hospital (62 patients presented over a year), the yearly rate of lung surgery rose by 30% after video meetings with a London chest-surgery centre began; it is a single before-and-after study.
supported_en: A 2004 study from Southend (UK, 62 patients presented over a year) found the yearly rate of lung surgery rose by 30% after video team meetings with a surgical centre began.
not_supported_en: The 2004 study does not show the effect on the share of all patients who get curative treatment, and nothing shows it in a Finnish setting.
in_use_summary_en: OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says the university hospital is responsible for the lung cancer team meetings, where treatment plans are made, and for surgery and radiotherapy.
missing_en: No page shows that every Lapland stage I-III patient is discussed by video with the OYS team before a decision against curative treatment.
summary_en: B: OYS's lung cancer care-pathway page says the university hospital is responsible for the lung cancer team meetings and for surgery and radiotherapy, and that treatment plans are made in that meeting. No Lapha or OYS page shows that every Lapland stage I-III patient is discussed by video before a decision against curative treatment. A: One UK district hospital (Southend, 2004) reported a 30% rise in lung surgery after video meetings with a surgical centre began, which is weaker support for the assumed 1.5 points.
unanswered_en: I looked for, but did not find, a page from Lapha or OYS describing a video link from Lapin keskussairaala or Länsi-Pohja to the OYS lung cancer meeting, or a rule that every stage I-III patient must be reviewed there.

verdict_en: Partly in place in the OYS university hospital area, which treats Lapland's patients. Missing: No page shows that every Lapland stage I-III patient is discussed by video with the OYS team before a decision against curative treatment. Evidence supports that it works, but not the size of effect we assume. Supported: A 2004 study from Southend (UK, 62 patients presented over a year) found the yearly rate of lung surgery rose by 30% after video team meetings with a surgical centre began. Not supported: The 2004 study does not show the effect on the share of all patients who get curative treatment, and nothing shows it in a Finnish setting.
